title: Elimination of the penny will cost us as merchants and consumers
summary:
随着美国财政部逐步停用 1 美分硬币，企业和消费者正面临一系列新挑战，最终可能导致每个人的实际支出增加。这是因为，取消 1 美分硬币远没有想象中那么简单，这一举措正在催生一种双轨制的支付体系，即使用现金的消费者与使用借记卡、信用卡或数字钱包等电子支付的消费者，将在交易中被区别对待。由此引发了多方面的法律与监管担忧，包括消费者是否受到不公平对待，以及税收能否准确核算等问题。尽管许多细节仍有待进一步明确，但结论已经十分清楚：在结账时，我们所有人都可能要为此多付一些钱。

来源：芝加哥论坛报；作者：ROB KARR；原文发布时间：2026-01-02 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: As the U.S. Treasury phases out the use of the penny, it’s creating a host of new challenges for businesses and consumers that could cost all of us a good chunk of change. That’s because eliminating the 1-cent piece is more complicated than it seems, creating a two-tier system that treats customers who pay with cash differently than customers who pay electronically, whether that be with a debit or credit card or a digital wallet. This raises a host of legal and regulatory concerns, from unequal treatment of consumers to proper tax collection. While there’s still a lot to figure out, the bottom line is clear: We’ll all be paying more when it comes time to check out.
paragraphs.contentZh: 随着美国财政部逐步停用 1 美分硬币，企业和消费者正面临一系列新挑战，最终可能导致每个人的实际支出增加。这是因为，取消 1 美分硬币远没有想象中那么简单，这一举措正在催生一种双轨制的支付体系，即使用现金的消费者与使用借记卡、信用卡或数字钱包等电子支付的消费者，将在交易中被区别对待。由此引发了多方面的法律与监管担忧，包括消费者是否受到不公平对待，以及税收能否准确核算等问题。尽管许多细节仍有待进一步明确，但结论已经十分清楚：在结账时，我们所有人都可能要为此多付一些钱。

paragraphs.contentEn: The crux of the problem is rounding. As pennies exit circulation, it is becoming increasingly difficult for retailers to make exact change for cash transactions. Without pennies, cash transactions will have to either be rounded up to the nearest 5 cents or down to the nearest 5 cents. Because federal and state officials have not provided guidance on the issue, businesses are left to set their own rounding policies.
paragraphs.contentZh: 问题的关键在于取整机制。随着 1 美分硬币退出流通，零售商在现金交易中越来越难做到精准找零。在没有 1 美分硬币的情况下，现金结账金额只能被向上进位或是向下抹零来取整至最接近的 5 美分。然而，由于联邦和州政府尚未就这一问题给出明确指引，商家目前只能自行决定具体的取整规则。

paragraphs.contentEn: The law of uniform distribution tells us that over many transactions, there are likely to be as many transactions that are rounded down as rounded up. But this scenario disproportionately affects consumers who rely on cash, the majority of whom come from lower-income households or are adults over the age of 55, according to Federal Reserve Financial Services. There are still implications for customers who pay with a card or electronic payment, however. If rounding only applies to cash transactions, consumers paying with a card may be penalized as they are required to pay the exact amount while those paying with cash may have their transactions rounded down to the nearest nickel, depending on the total cost of a transaction.
paragraphs.contentZh: 根据均匀分布原理，在大量交易中，向上进位与向下抹零的情况理论上应大致各占一半。但美联储金融服务部门的数据显示，这种取整机制对依赖现金的消费者（主要是低收入家庭或 55 岁以上的中老年人）的影响并不均衡。与此同时，使用银行卡或电子支付的消费者同样会受到影响。如果取整规则仅适用于现金交易，刷卡支付的消费者反而可能面临一种变相的惩罚，因为他们必须支付精确到分的金额，而现金支付者则可能会根据交易总额，被向下抹零凑整到最接近的 5 美分。

paragraphs.contentEn: This uneven treatment not only raises questions of fairness, but the lack of guidance from federal and local government also leaves retailers at risk of violating sales and excise tax collection rules and consumer protection regulations. It’s an untenable and unfair position for businesses, even as retailers do their part to adjust to the exit of the penny responsibly, including communicating with customers about what they should expect at the register.
paragraphs.contentZh: 这种差异化处理不仅引发了公平性问题，更关键的是，由于联邦和地方政府尚未提供明确指引，零售商还可能面临违反销售税和消费税征收规定，以及消费者保护法规的风险。虽然零售商仍在努力以负责任的方式应对 1 美分硬币退出流通的现实，例如提前向消费者说明结账时可能出现的变化，但目前商家仍陷入了一种既难以持续、又难以保证公平的困境。

paragraphs.contentEn: Consider this real-world scenario: Under federal law, those receiving Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits cannot be treated differently than non-SNAP recipients. Because SNAP benefits are loaded onto debit cards, they are processed as an electronic transaction. That means SNAP recipients will pay the exact amount for an item, whereas their non-SNAP counterparts paying with cash may have their total rounded down. This puts retailers in direct conflict with federal law. Though the Illinois Retail Merchants Association is working to educate state and federal officials on needed policy updates caused by the phaseout of the penny, it will take time before changes can be put in place. In the meantime, retailers are being forced to take on costly regulatory and compliance risks.
paragraphs.contentZh: 来看一个现实案例：联邦法律规定，补充营养援助计划（SNAP，即食品券）的受益人不得与非受益人受到不同对待。由于 SNAP 福利通过借记卡发放，因此在使用时会被视作电子支付。也就是说，SNAP 受益人需按商品的精确金额支付；而使用现金的非 SNAP 受益人，其交易总额却可能被向下抹零。这种差异使零售商直接面临违反联邦法律的风险。尽管伊利诺伊州零售商协会正在向州和联邦层面的官员说明情况，推动因 1 美分硬币退出流通所需的政策更新，但这些调整仍需时间才能落实。在此期间，零售商不得不承担成本高昂的监管和合规风险。

paragraphs.contentEn: Meanwhile, as more consumers choose to pay electronically rather than with cash to avoid the hassle of rounding, they’ll also be on the hook for more payment processing fees. That’s because each time a card is swiped or tapped, retailers are charged fees by card processing companies. In 2023 alone, these companies collected more than $172 billion in payment processing fees, most of which is passed on to consumers in the form of higher prices.
paragraphs.contentZh: 与此同时，为避开取整的麻烦，越来越多消费者开始改用电子支付而非现金结账，但这同时也意味着他们需要承担更高的支付手续费。原因在于，每一次刷卡或感应支付，商家都会被支付处理机构收取一笔费用。仅在 2023 年，这类机构收取的支付处理费就超过 1720 亿美元，而这部分成本的绝大部分，最终又会通过商品涨价转嫁给消费者。

paragraphs.contentEn: Our association has led the way in limiting these fees — securing passage of the first law in the nation to prohibit banks and credit card companies from charging processing fees on the tax and tip portion of a transaction — but Wall Street banks, credit card companies and card processors are fighting these consumer protections in court. Regardless of the outcome of that case, the transition away from the penny will only increase the use of digital payment methods and the accompanying fees. Eliminating the penny may seem like a small change, but businesses and customers will feel the impact long after the coin disappears.
paragraphs.contentZh: 我们协会在限制交易手续费方面一直走在前列——曾推动通过全美首部相关法律，明确规定银行和信用卡公司不得对交易中的税费及小费部分收取处理费——但华尔街的大型银行、信用卡公司以及支付处理机构正通过司法途径，对这些消费者保护措施提出挑战。无论这起案件最终结果如何，1 美分硬币的退出都只会进一步推高数字支付的使用频率，并带来更多随之而来的手续费成本。取消 1 美分硬币看似只是一个微小的变动，但其带来的连锁反应，将在硬币退出流通后，让企业与消费者在很长一段时间内持续感受到切实的影响。
